newsitem.title: USA: Matria gets expanded marketing for test.
newsitem.headline: Matria gets expanded marketing for test.

text.p: Matria Healthcare Inc said Monday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted approval to expand marketing of its test for predicting the risk of preterm delivery to women without symptoms of preterm labor.
The fetal fibronectin immunoassay test received approval in 1995 for use in women following the development of preterm labor symptoms between the 24th and 34th week of pregnancy.
The immunoassay is the first and only biochemical marker approved for use in predicting the risk of preterm delivery, the company said.

Asymptomatic patients, or women without symptoms of preterm labor, who had positive test results had greater risk than patients in the general population of delivering before 35 weeks gestation, the company said.
Matria has exclusive marketing rights to the test in the United States through a contract with Adeza Biomedical Corp it said. The company was not immediately available to comment further.
